The fix is in place and verified.

**What changed** — only `src/slugify.mjs`:

```js
export function slugify(input) {
  return String(input)
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "");
}
```

The original only collapsed whitespace runs (`/\s+/g`), so punctuation such as `,`, `!`, `++`, and `&` leaked through and leading/trailing spaces became hyphens. The new pattern replaces every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen, then strips hyphens from both ends.

**Verification** — I ran the module directly under Node and all cases passed:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `'Hello, World!'` | `hello-world` |
| `'  A  B  '` | `a-b` |
| `'C++ & Rust'` | `c-rust` |
| `''` / `'---'` | `''` |
| `'already-slug'` | `already-slug` |
| `'Node.js v24.14.0'` | `node-js-v24-14-0` |
